definition: ask_coverage — an ask that DECLARES its own parts must be answered in every part. Parts are declared three ways and no other: a bullet block of at least two list items, an inline enumeration of at least two markers in ascending sequence ((1), (a), i)), or an ordinal-word sequence (first … second … finally). Sentence boundaries and connectors are NOT part boundaries — a writer who numbers their questions is declaring that these are separate things, and a full stop declares nothing. A part is MEASURABLE when it carries at least two content terms, at least one of which names a subject rather than a manner of answering (cite, source, point, spec, example …), and when it is not itself a manner clause (answer from…, keep it…). A measurable part is COVERED when at least two of its distinct content terms are engaged by the output (exact, stemmed, or sharing a four-character prefix), OR the part carried an ordinal the output mirrors, OR the part asks for prose with a produce verb (draft, write, summarise …) and the output carries at least forty words — because an output that IS the requested reply cannot be recognised as one lexically. The rule FAILS when at least one measurable part is uncovered, and SKIPS when there is no input, when the output is empty, when the input exceeds 1500 characters, or when fewer than two parts can be measured. Definitions: src/eval/text/asks.ts; rule: src/eval/rules/completeness.ts. Positive = a reader of the ask and the answer would say a declared part was not addressed (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-05 for arc 4. One case carries the shape of real transcript t-19 (a three-part enumerated question answered in one part). Three negatives exist because the design FAILED them against the real transcripts before this file was written and was corrected: a meta-ask with no subject ("Cite a source"), a manner clause ("Answer from the engine source, not the docs"), and an answer that performs the ask rather than describing it (a drafted reply). Every case declares its parts and every case is one the rule JUDGES — none skips, because the proof runner scores a skip as not-failed.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled against the documented definition above on 2026-09-05, by reading the ask against the answer and asking whether a reader would say a declared part went unaddressed — never by counting terms. Each note states which clause decided the label. Cases the measurement then disagrees with are reported as errors, not relabelled. Two failure modes are stated rather than discovered later: a declared part answered in wholly different words, with no ordinal mirrored and no produce verb, reads as uncovered; and a genuinely multi-part ask written as flowing prose is not judged at all.

cases.label: positive
cases.input: Three things: (1) what port does the dashboard bind by default, (2) which config key changes the retention window, and (3) does the traces endpoint move with the port?
cases.output: The dashboard binds port 6920 by default, set in the dashboard block of the configuration.
cases.notes: Three enumerated parts, one addressed. Neither the retention window nor the traces endpoint appears in any words. FAIL.

cases.label: positive
cases.input: Tell me (1) how many built-in rules there are, (2) which bundle each rule belongs to, and (3) which rules are critical by default.
cases.output: There are seventeen built-in rules.
cases.notes: The count is given; the bundle mapping and the critical list are absent. FAIL.

cases.label: positive
cases.input: Please cover (1) how the retention sweep is scheduled, (2) what records it deletes, and (3) how an operator disables it.
cases.output: The sweep runs on a timer at boot and again every twenty-four hours, on an unref-ed interval so it never holds the process open.
cases.notes: Scheduling is answered thoroughly. Thoroughness on one part does not cover the other two. FAIL.

cases.notes: A bulleted three-part ask. The first bullet is answered well; the keys and their ruling status are never mentioned. FAIL.

cases.input: First explain what a skip means. Second, explain how a skip differs from a pass. Finally, say what a gate should do about one.
cases.output: A skip means the rule was never asked, because the input it needed was absent. It differs from a pass in that a pass is a judgement and a skip is the absence of one.
cases.notes: Three ordinal words, the last dropped. FAIL.

Hi Devraj,

Yes — the personal-data rule is label-anchored and matches an ISO date as well as the slash form, so an intake record carrying DOB: 1991-04-17 is caught. The stored trace text is redacted only when you turn redaction on.

Support
cases.notes: THE PERFORMED ASK: the output IS the drafted reply, and no lexical test can see that. A produce-verb part discharged by substantial prose reads as covered, which resolves the ambiguity in the direction this rule always resolves it. PASS.
